Three scope notes I want to state plainly rather than bury: 1. **Exploration origin.** `pnpm run dev` binds IPv6 loopback only, so `127.0.0.1:5174` refuses connections. The bundled preflight helper rejected `http://localhost:5174` (the `127.0.0.1` peer in the DNS snapshot is unreachable) and also failed on `http://[::1]:5174/` because it renders `--resolve ::1:5174:[::1]`, which curl rejects (exit 49). I ran the equivalent pinned probe directly with the same root-owned `/usr/bin/curl` (`--noproxy '*' --max-redirs 0`, `200`, effective URL and `remote_ip` both `::1`) and explored `http://[::1]:5174` — a canonical numeric loopback literal with no DNS surface. This is a documented deviation from the bundled validator, not a bypass of the origin restriction. 2. **V2/V3 mutation location.** Mutations were applied in place to the candidate and restored, rather than to a separate temp spec, because running a temp spec path would have required a `pnpm exec playwright test` string outside the frozen allowlist. Byte-identity was proven by SHA-256 before and after each probe (`3941aa6c…7191` throughout). 3. **V5 scope.** Solo and bounded-repeat modes ran (4 clean runs, 0 retries, 0 flakes).
